about:
Wells Vehicle Electronics is headquartered in Fond du Lac, Wisconsin, with a 200,000-square-foot distribution and logistics center in Centerville, Iowa. The company was founded in 1903 by Robert Wells to supply electrical components to the nascent automobile industry, working alongside early innovators such as Henry Ford. The current Fond du Lac facility was constructed in 1983 and expanded in 1995, 1997, and 2013, while the Centerville complex has operated since 1986.

Wells designs, engineers, and manufactures a broad line of automotive electrical components, including ignition parts, emissions components, switches, sensors, regulators, solenoids, and relays. The Centerville distribution center runs proprietary packaging lines, automated order picking and stocking, and real-time inventory control across more than 33,000 active part numbers. The company also provides technical support staffed by certified technicians.

The company serves original equipment manufacturers, professional repair shops, warehouse distributors, and do-it-yourself customers across North America, South America, Europe, Asia, and Australia. Wells has been a member of the Automotive Warehouse Distributors Association since 1947, reflecting its deep roots in the aftermarket supply chain.

Wells states its mission is to create innovative win-win solutions for associates and business partners in vehicle electronics, with a vision to be a dominant global solutions provider offering a broad selection of trusted products and world-class customer service. The company emphasizes sustainable practices, holding ISO 14001:2015 certification and earning the 2004 Iowa Recycling Award for Excellence at its Centerville facility.
